precepts.text: Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet at the laver.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Where did the washing come from? Exodus 30:19: “For Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat”. The priests washed at the laver. This is where John the Baptist got it from.

Isaiah shows what the washing symbolized: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. The water was a symbol of putting away evil.

John the Baptist did not make up water baptism. It came from the priests, and John was in the lineage of the priesthood; he was a Levite. So the doctrine of baptisms that Hebrews 6 says to leave is the priests' washing, one of the old ordinances Christ, the new high priest, brought to an end.

precepts.text: On the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls, and the priest makes an atonement to cleanse the children of Israel from all their sins, an everlasting statute.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
Aaron made atonement upon the horns of the incense altar “once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements”. This altar served the day of atonement, and Leviticus 16 lays that day out.

“And this shall be a statute for ever unto you: that in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and do no work at all”. On that day the priest made an atonement “for the holy sanctuary”, “for the tabernacle of the congregation, and for the altar”, and “for the priests, and for all the people of the congregation”, “to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before the Lord.”

“And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make an atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year.” Once a year: that is the once in a year of Exodus 30:10.

precepts.text: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
“Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people”.

That once every year is the day of atonement, when Aaron made atonement upon the horns of the altar with the blood of the sin offering of atonements, for himself, for the priests and for all the people. The high priest went in alone, and not without blood.

precepts.text: The daily sacrifices can never take away sins, but this man offered one sacrifice for sins for ever and sat down on the right hand of God.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
“And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God”. “we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.”

So the day of atonement is still kept: the tenth day of the seventh month, afflicting the soul and doing no work at all, an everlasting statute. But it is kept without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal. The blood of the sin offering of atonements that Aaron put on the horns of the altar once in a year has been answered by one sacrifice for sins for ever.

precepts.text: Aaron shall burn a perpetual sweet incense throughout your generations, and no strange incense; the law of the incense was already set.
precepts.point: The fire that went out from the Lord was the same fire that came out from before the Lord in Leviticus 9 and consumed the burnt offering upon the altar.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
The instructions for the incense were already given before Nadab and Abihu ever took up their censers. “And Aaron shall burn thereon sweet incense every morning: when he dresseth the lamps, he shall burn incense upon it. And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at even, he shall burn incense upon it, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations.”

And the restriction: “Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon, nor burnt sacrifice, nor meat offering; neither shall ye pour drink offering thereon.” There were instructions on what could be burned and what could not. The strange fire is that Nadab and Abihu put strange incense before the Lord, “which he commanded them not.”

When the Most High gave instructions through Moses on what to sacrifice and how, it was with specificity; you were to do it exactly the way he told you. The law of the incense was already set, and they went outside it.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
A laver of brass, with a brass foot, is set between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar and filled with water. Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet before entering or approaching the altar to minister. “they shall wash with water, that they die not”. Washing for this service is a statute through their generations.

The pictured vessel has water filling the upper part and coming from the mouths of the brass oxen, filling the area where the Levites washed. Its size is apparent beside the men. This water and washing help explain the sea like crystal before the throne.

The Pharisees took the washing required for service in the tabernacle and temple and applied it as a law in the street. That is the issue with the handwashing dispute mentioned in Matthew 15. It is not permission to walk around eating with dirty hands; the point is that the temple requirement was being imposed outside its appointed setting.

points: Once in a year, with the blood of the sin offering of atonements.

note.label: Day of Atonement

points: The altar to burn incense upon was made of shittim wood, a cubit in length and a cubit in breadth, foursquare, and two cubits high, with horns of the same. A cubit has been read to be about seventeen inches, so this stood about waist high.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: It was overlaid with pure gold, the top, the sides round about, and the horns, with a crown of gold round about, two golden rings under the crown, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold. The staves through the rings were how the priests bore it as Israel moved through the wilderness.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The altar was put before the vail that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat where the Most High would meet with Moses.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Aaron burned sweet incense on it every morning when he dressed the lamps, and again at even when he lighted the lamps, a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout the generations; it burned continually, morning and evening.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: No strange incense went on it, and no burnt sacrifice, meat offering, or drink offering; this altar was for one specific incense only. The service had to be exactly as prescribed, and deviation carried death, which is a reason to thank the Lord for Christ.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Aaron made an atonement upon the horns of it once in a year with the blood of the sin offering of atonements; it is most holy unto the Lord. This altar served the day of atonement.

On the tenth day of the seventh month Israel afflicted their souls and did no work at all, and the priest made an atonement for the sanctuary, the tabernacle, the altar, the priests, and all the people of the congregation, to cleanse them from all their sins before the Lord; an everlasting statute, once a year.

The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Numbering the children of Israel was not done lightly; when they were counted, every man gave a ransom for his soul unto the Lord, that there be no plague among them when they were numbered.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The ransom was half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary, from every one that passed among them that were numbered, from twenty years old and above; the rich gave no more and the poor gave no less, to make an atonement for their souls.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The atonement money was appointed for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation. The gold, the wood, the curtains, and the fabrics all had to be bought and kept up, and the tabernacle moved with the nation through the wilderness; that is the same reason offerings are gathered in the congregation today, because the house of the Most High cannot be built or kept without it.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The laver of brass, with his foot also of brass, stood between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar, with water in it; a great brass bowl set on a brass base.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet thereat when they went into the tabernacle of the congregation and when they came near to the altar to minister, that they die not; the priests could not go in unclean.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: It was a statute for ever to Aaron and to his seed throughout their generations.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The holy anointing oil was compounded of principal spices, pure myrrh five hundred shekels, sweet cinnamon two hundred and fifty, sweet calamus two hundred and fifty, cassia five hundred after the shekel of the sanctuary, and oil olive an hin, an ointment compound after the art of the apothecary, which is a maker of perfume.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: With it were anointed the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the table and all his vessels, the candlestick and his vessels, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his vessels, and the laver and his foot, that they be most holy; whatsoever toucheth them shall be holy. Aaron and his sons were anointed and consecrated with it to minister in the priest's office.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: It was not poured upon man's flesh, and none was to be made like it after the composition of it; whosoever compounded any like it, or put any of it upon a stranger, was cut off from his people.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: The perfume was made of sweet spices, stacte, onycha, and galbanum, with pure frankincense, of each a like weight, tempered together, pure and holy, a confection after the art of the apothecary.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: Part of it was beaten very small and put before the testimony in the tabernacle of the congregation; unto you it shall be most holy. The Most High wanted the tabernacle anointed and smelling sweet, everything done one specific way.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

points: It was for the Lord alone; ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof, and whosoever made like unto it, to smell thereto, was cut off from his people. There were no knockoffs of the holy things; a copy carried death.
